# Fixtures

Small synthetic DXF drawings, generated by [gen/generate.py](gen/generate.py) and committed.

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv                                   # from the repo root, once
.venv/bin/pip install -r test/fixtures/requirements.txt
.venv/bin/python test/fixtures/gen/generate.py          # all of them
.venv/bin/python test/fixtures/gen/generate.py lines    # or just one
```

**Python is only needed to add or change a fixture.** The `.dxf` files are committed, so `npm test`
runs with node alone.

## Why synthetic

`test-data/` holds a hundred real drawings, and they are the better test — but they are customer
and user-reported files that cannot be redistributed, so CI cannot see them. These can be
committed, each is small enough to reason about, and the function that generates one says what it
is for, which a binary `.dxf` never can.

The two corpora do different jobs and neither replaces the other: fixtures give exact expected
output, `test-data/` gives real-world pathology.

## Rules

- **Keep coordinates within [-100, 100].** Scene vertices are float32, whose absolute error at that
  magnitude is about 8e-6 — comfortably inside the 1e-4 that the dumps round to. Larger coordinates
  would make the goldens sensitive to float32 rounding rather than to real change.
- **Prefer coordinates that are exact in binary** (integers, halves), so a golden can be read
  against the call that produced it.
- **Keep each drawing minimal.** One or two entities exercising one path. A fixture that is hard to
  read is a golden nobody will review.
- **Regeneration must be byte-stable.** ezdxf varies GUIDs and timestamps per run; `_Normalize` and
  `_Write` pin them. CI regenerates and runs `git diff --exit-code`, so anything else that varies
  will show up there. `ezdxf` is pinned in `requirements.txt` for the same reason.
- **Audit new fixtures** — `ezdxf.readfile(path).audit()` should report nothing, so a malformed
  file is never enshrined as expected behavior.

## Known limits

- **No text.** The dump harness supplies no font fetchers, so TEXT, MTEXT, ATTRIB and DIMENSION
  produce no geometry. Text fixtures need fonts in the repo first.
- **ezdxf is not an oracle here.** Its own renderer models text and lineweights differently, so it
  can be used for a side-by-side sanity check but never for pixel or geometry equality. The goldens
  record what *this* library does; correctness is judged by reading them, and against
  https://viewer.autodesk.com when in doubt.
- Every drawing carries a `Defpoints` layer, which ezdxf creates. It is harmless and is why the
  layer count is one higher than the fixture defines.
